window_notes: Andalucia GIP table olive. Patch: 1 adult/McPhail/day or 3 adults/chromotropic/day AND first stung fruit. Table-olive stung fruit is unfit for processing.
action: Whole-tree larvicide treatment; patch bait treatment at first stung fruit

window_notes: Andalucia 2024 strategy notes: in PI, lambda-cyhalothrin products only against the autumn generation and always before 31 October; deltamethrin max 2 applications in PI. Label PHI governs (7-28 d by product).
action: Schedule last PI pyrethroid application before 31 Oct and check PHI vs harvest date

window_notes: CLM 2025 season: McPhail max provincial mean 24.07/trap/day in Toledo early Oct (about 4 elsewhere); chromotropic max 9.15 (Toledo) and 2.12 (Cuenca) late Oct; max provincial mean stung viable fruit 35.7% north Cuenca, about 8% elsewhere. NO regulatory CLM treatment threshold retrieved (CLM PI order not found).
action: Use regional ERAA bulletin / OCA / ASV trap data; no automatic spray trigger

window_notes: AEMET alert level (human impact) not crop-damage threshold. Yellow/orange/red: 38/40/44 in Guadalquivir, Sierra, Badajoz, Valle del Tajo, La Mancha Ciudad Real/Toledo; 36/39/42 in La Mancha albaceteña, Alcarria conquense, norte de Cáceres, Valencia/Cataluña interior. Crop damage threshold for olive fruit NAV.
action: Irrigate to full ETc where available for the heat spell; avoid pruning and N fertiliser; kaolin where used

duration: pit hardening to oil accumulation (minimum tolerated in trial)
window_notes: EVIDENCE=field trial Cyprus, Koroneiki, low density, one high-crop year (Agric. Water Manag. 258:107200): 35% ETc at pit hardening+oil accumulation (70% elsewhere) gave same yield/oil quality as 70% sustained. Not Spain; not intensive/hedgerow; trigger on soil/plant water status NAV.
action: If water is limiting, protect fruit-growth/oil-accumulation supply at or above 35% ETc rather than cutting evenly; validate for Spanish cultivars

window_notes: AEMET yellow/orange/red 12h = 40/80/120 mm; inland (Andalucia, CLM, Extremadura, Lleida). Meteoalerta v1 31-May-2022 (check current plan).
action: Check drainage/runoff channels and culverts, plan machinery access

action: Open drainage, keep traffic off wet soil, move harvest/treatment plan

window_notes: AEMET yellow/orange/red 70/90/130 km/h in most olive zones (80/100/140 Serranía de Cuenca). Fruit-drop damage threshold NAV.
action: Prioritise exposed plots for harvest; secure nets/equipment

window_notes: AEMET defines 'strong' storms (yellow) as including hail >1 cm; 'very strong' (orange) hail >2 cm. Wounds are entry points for Pseudomonas savastanoi (UC IPM). Hail-damaged-fruit % trigger for early harvest NAV.
action: Photograph/document damage for Agroseguro; inspect fruit/wounds after the event

window_notes: As HAIL-01, orange level.
action: Same plus copper protectant on wounds promptly after hail (guidance from knot guides; the 24 h figure comes from a secondary guide, low confidence)

window_notes: EVIDENCE=field-observational, from review (Petruccelli et al. 2022); setting not specified. Autumn drop from -0.4 to -3 C before harvest: dehydration/wilting, brown blisters, internal browning, some fully frozen fruit, reduced oil accumulation. NOT lab.
action: Forecast <= -0.4 C: harvest the most exposed/cold-pocket plots first; after the event, cut sample fruit for browning

window_notes: EVIDENCE=LAB ONLY: Arbequina, Chile (Atacama), harvested fruit frozen post-harvest at -3+/-1 C for 12 h then thawed: lower phenols/ORAC, 'frostbitten' sensory defect (low intensity), hexanal +34% in June. Authors warn natural frost may differ. Do NOT use as a field air-temperature trigger; irrigation 86-110% ET0 / K2O 100-107 only modelled mitigation for phenols (low R2).
action: Reference only: use FROST-01 for field alerts

window_notes: AEMET minimum temp yellow/orange/red: -4/-8/-12 in interior Andalucia (Sierra, Jaén, Granada interior, Cordoba Sierra/Subbetica), CLM (Albacete, Ciudad Real, Toledo), Extremadura, Lleida, Tarragona depresion, Valencia interior sur; -1/-4/-8 in Campina cordobesa/sevillana and coast; -6/-10/-14 Cuenca and interior norte Valencia. Warning level is colder than field drupe injury onset: do not rely on AEMET warning alone.
action: Escalate FROST-01 actions to urgent; no further fertilisation/pruning

duration: wetness up to 48 h raises severity
window_notes: EVIDENCE=lab+field (Moral et al. 2012, C. acutatum/simmondsii): infection 10-25 C, shortest latency and highest severity about 17-20 C; severity rises with wetness to 48 h; infection of maturing fruit (veraison to harvest). Minimum wetness hours not in abstract.
action: Flag high-risk window after rain; plan early harvest of susceptible cultivars (Arbequina tolerance low); copper timing per regional PI guide NAV

window_notes: EVIDENCE=oil-extraction trial with inoculated batches, Arbequina and Frantoio, Crop Prot. 2018: Arbequina <=13% incidence (severity<1.5); Frantoio <=50% (severity<2; abstract also says range 0-30%, check full paper). Sensory limits may be lower.
action: If Arbequina batch >13% anthracnose: bring harvest forward, segregate and mill rejected lot separately

window_notes: RAIF Málaga bulletin 14-18 Oct 2024: 8-24 C favours Spilocaea oleagina, optimum 20 C, optimum RH 100%; strategy is preventive. Lab (Viruega et al. 2011 abstract, via search snippet; page 403): infection 5-25 C, max severity about 20 C with 12-24 h wetness, about 15 C with longer wetness.
action: Preventive fungicide only when conditions are favourable; check incubated/visible leaf spots; prune for aeration

window_notes: PI autumn rule retrieved only qualitatively (RAIF: check visible/incubated spots before treating once conditions are favourable). Numeric trigger sits in the PI Reglamento (not retrieved; Andalucia 2026 draft Order exists). Observed Malaga means Oct 2024: 0.7% visible, 1.7% incubated (not thresholds).
action: Sample leaves (visible + incubated by NaOH test), treat per PI guide

window_notes: Field-observational (see OLV-S08-FROST-01). Prevention action only.
action: Bring forward harvest of exposed plots and mill promptly; irrigation or potassium as frost mitigation is lab-modelled only (see FROST-02), not recommended as field action until validated

window_notes: After the event: sample fruit (cut for browning/flesh discoloration), harvest and mill frost-affected fruit in a separate lot to avoid contaminating EVOO ('frostbitten' defect, lab-demonstrated). Optimal hours-to-harvest after frost: NAV (draft's 24-48 h not supported by a source).
action: Inspect fruit; segregate frost-affected lots; decide EVOO vs lower grade by sensory/chemical check

window_notes: Inland zones (red 120). Coast/prelitoral Cataluna and Valencia: orange 100 mm (red 180); 1h orange 30 inland / 40 coast. Harvest-specific dry-spell/soil-moisture rules: NAV (not found in PI guides retrieved).
action: Harvest ripe plots before event; stop traffic on saturated soil; document for insurance

window_notes: Searched PI guides/RAIF/CLM bulletins and trade sources: no sourced dry-spell or mm/day threshold for shaker harvest. Trade note: growers typically wait 2-3 dry days (secondary source, not verified).
action: Re-sequence plots to dry windows; process within 24 h (practice)

window_notes: Fruit-drop effect threshold NAV; AEMET level only.
action: Harvest exposed plots first

variable: stung_fruit_percentage at harvest decision (Mediterranean action level)
duration: action threshold used in Mediterranean areas (as cited)
window_notes: Giacalone et al. cite 15% as the action threshold adopted in Mediterranean areas; Andalucia PI/GIP triggers are 5% (oil) and 1% (table) stung fruit and the draft's '10%' could not be verified. RAIF: advancing mill harvest to Oct-Nov limits damage because part of larvae are still inside fruit.
action: Advance harvest; segregate infested fruit; PHI check before any spray

window_notes: RAIF: tilling soil under canopy after harvest can reduce overwintering pupae; mass-trap devices installed in spring can stay all year (20 units/ha up to 35-50/ha in small plots).
action: Till under canopy after harvest where compatible with soil protection

window_notes: See OLV-S08-ANTH-02 (free acidity <0.8%).
action: Early harvest and quick milling; keep diseased fruit out of EVOO lot

window_notes: Moral et al. 2012; optimum 17-20 C. Wet harvest weeks keep infection going; infected fruit raises acidity.
action: Harvest early in wet autumns and speed up daily harvest rate

window_notes: Spilocaea spore density in lesions peaks Nov-Feb in favourable years, zero in summer; dispersal by rain splash (Picual orchard, S. Spain, 4 years).
action: Plan post-harvest protection for the Nov-Feb window

window_notes: Searched: no sourced pre-harvest irrigation rule for Spain; only the Cyprus RDI trial (see OLV-S08-DEFIC-01).
action: No recommendation without local validation

duration: wounds stay susceptible to Pseudomonas savastanoi (olive knot)
window_notes: EVIDENCE=California IPM guide: pruning wounds susceptible for at least 14 days; leaf scars about 7 days after leaf drop; spread by rain; dry-summer wounds not susceptible; excess freeze damage raises severity. Spanish PI duration NAV.
action: Prune only with 14 d dry outlook where possible; disinfect tools (10% bleach); copper bactericide after pruning/harvest per label

window_notes: Field-observational (review): 0 to -3 C slight damage to young organs; -6 to -7 C moderate damage to nearly all organs; below -12 to -18 C severe. AEMET warning -4/-8/-12 interior. Postponing pruning until real damage is visible is general practice (weakly sourced), so threshold NAV for pruning decision.
action: Delay pruning in cold interior zones until after main frost risk and damage assessment; restoration pruning after frost (Pannelli 2013 cited by review)

duration: no pruning debris left in field from 1 May
window_notes: RAIF: from 1 May to 31 Oct, where there is pruning wood, apply Ley 43/2002 measures (Orders 2-Nov-1981 and 10-Mar-1982) to prevent olive bark beetle Phloeotribus scarabaeoides; seal large pruning wounds in zones with history of damage.
action: Remove, burn (per rules) or store pruning wood before 1 May

window_notes: RAIF 14-18 Oct 2024 and Viruega 2011 abstract; preventive; cultural: aerating pruning, avoid N excess, resistant cultivars (Lechín de Sevilla, Manzanilla de Hellín, Picudo de Montoro). Copper dose/PI timing NAV (EU copper under review).
action: Aerating prune; post-harvest protective fungicide if favourable conditions and symptom counts justify

action: Drain, avoid traffic
